title: Magnets
lead: Magnetism begins with a fact anyone can check with two refrigerator magnets: every magnet has two ends that behave differently, and a magnet free to swing turns one of them toward the north. This section names those ends the north and south magnetic poles and looks at what they do to each other, to Earth, and to a magnet cut into pieces.
objectives: Describe the difference between the north and south poles of a magnet.
Describe how magnetic poles interact with each other.
summary_html:
• Magnetism is a subject that includes the properties of magnets, the effect of the magnetic force on moving charges and currents, and the creation of magnetic fields by currents.
  • There are two types of magnetic poles, called the north magnetic pole and south magnetic pole.
  • North magnetic poles are those that are attracted toward the Earth’s geographic north pole.
  • Like poles repel and unlike poles attract.
  • Magnetic poles always occur in pairs of north and south—it is not possible to isolate north and south poles.

exercises.prompt: Volcanic and other such activity at the mid-Atlantic ridge extrudes material to fill the gap between separating tectonic plates associated with continental drift. The magnetization of rocks is found to reverse in a coordinated manner with distance from the ridge. What does this imply about the Earth’s magnetic field and how could the knowledge of the spreading rate be used to give its historical record?

answer.solution: Rock that cools at the ridge takes on the direction of Earth’s field at the moment it hardens and then keeps it. The sea floor therefore carries a record of that direction, laid down strip by strip as the plates move apart. Bands of opposite magnetization at increasing distances from the ridge imply that Earth’s field has reversed many times. The end of Earth’s magnet that is now a south magnetic pole near the geographic North Pole has at times been a north magnetic pole instead. The two plates move apart at a measurable rate, so dividing the distance from the ridge to a band by that rate gives the time since the band formed, and the sequence of bands becomes a dated history of the reversals.
